finding: Line 38 still says `ResolveOverrideFocus` "reads it and emits the \"matches no active role\" warning itself", which directly contradicts §2.6's "The §2.3 warnings are buffered, not written, while the checks run". An implementer following §2.2 literally puts an `output.Info` inside `ResolveOverrideFocus` and breaks the buffering on the first line of the change. The sentence is also inaccurate against the current tree, where both call sites take a returned warning slice and the caller prints it (internal/cli/audit.go:234, internal/cli/review.go:662).

resolved.evidence: CONFIRMED, and the citation was wrong about the code rather than merely inconsistent. ResolveOverrideFocus RETURNS warnings (internal/engine/overrides.go:19) and review.go:662-664 emits them. §2.2 now says it returns the warning to its caller, which emits it.

finding: The buffering rule is written against a warning channel that is silent in the mode it will be exercised in. The §2.3 "matches no active role" warning is emitted through output.Info (internal/cli/review.go:657-665, internal/cli/audit.go:234), and output.Info returns immediately when jsonMode is set (internal/output/output.go:150-156), which Configure/EnsureConfigured set whenever stdout is not a TTY or --json is passed — i.e. every agent-facing invocation and every CLI test (internal/cli/commands_test.go:38-41 prepends --json to every runTP call). Buffered-then-discarded and buffered-then-flushed therefore produce byte-identical output, so §6 item 8's "fixture that can fail it" cannot fail: the warning is absent from the refused run and from the one-role-active run alike. The tree already concedes this — internal/cli/domain_lens_test.go:187-189 delegates the warning text to the engine test because the CLI harness cannot see it. As written the implementer must invent an observation channel (emit these warnings regardless of jsonMode, route them into the JSON payload, or run the fixture without --json) with no guidance on which.

resolved.evidence: CONFIRMED. Round 10 deleted §2.6's buffering rule and the §6 item that tested it: the §2.3 warnings travel output.Info, which returns early whenever stdout is not a terminal, so the rule described suppressing something already silent and the test could not fail. §2.6 now states only what a refusal guarantees — no prompt emitted, no state written — and explicitly specifies nothing about the advisory warnings.

suggestion: State in §2.6 which channel the buffered warnings travel on and that it is suppressed under --json/piped output, then pin the observation: either (a) require item 8's fixture to run without --json (TTY/non-JSON invocation) and assert the stderr text, or (b) make the buffer a unit-level return value asserted in an engine/CLI-helper test, or (c) declare that under --json the rule is vacuous and item 8 asserts only exit 2 plus empty stdout — dropping the 'fixture that can fail it' claim.

finding: Round 9 recorded the round-8 high (the `spec-coverage` refusal keys on §2.3's drop set rather than on the frontmatter entry, with no test that discriminates the two readings) as fixed with the evidence "Item 15 now holds the frontmatter IDENTICAL and varies only the corpus — spec-coverage.json present versus a populated auditor corpus without it". finding: The new item 8 — this round's flagship repair, added to give §2.6's buffering rule a fixture that can fail — cannot fail either, for the reason round 9 reported and this round's resolution answered by pointing at item 8. The §2.3 warnings are emitted through `output.Info` (internal/cli/review.go:657-659,663-665; internal/cli/audit.go:229-231,235-237); `output.Info` returns immediately when `jsonMode` is set (internal/output/output.go:150-156), and `jsonMode` is set whenever stdout is not a terminal (output.go:19). tp's CLI harness runs the binary as a subprocess with a piped stdout and always passes `--json` (internal/cli/commands_test.go:38-41), so no CLI test in this repo can observe a §2.3 warning at all — which is why the existing override test defers the warning text to an engine test (internal/cli/domain_lens_test.go:187-189). Item 8's first half ("the warning is discarded, not written") therefore passes against an eager-writing implementation exactly as item 7's removed clause did, and its second half ("the same spec with one role left active flushes the warning and proceeds") asserts output nothing can see. `output.Notice` (output.go:174-187) exists precisely for advisories that must survive jsonMode, but no section routes the flushed buffer to it.

resolved.evidence: CONFIRMED, same root cause as finding 1. Round 10 deleted §2.6's buffering rule and the §6 item that tested it: the §2.3 warnings travel output.Info, which returns early whenever stdout is not a terminal, so the rule described suppressing something already silent and the test could not fail. §2.6 now states only what a refusal guarantees — no prompt emitted, no state written — and explicitly specifies nothing about the advisory warnings.

suggestion: Name the emission channel in §2.6 — flush the buffer through `output.Notice` (or the same stream the refusal uses) so a piped run can observe it — and state what item 8 asserts on: either the Notice text on stderr, or an engine-level assertion over the returned buffer plus a CLI assertion that the refused run's stderr contains only the error object.

finding: "A non-boolean `enabled`" (§2.2, tested by §6 item 4) never says which YAML scalars are non-boolean, so item 4's fixture is unspecified and two engineers write contradictory tests. The repo parses frontmatter with gopkg.in/yaml.v3 (YAML 1.2 core schema), under which `enabled: no` and `enabled: off` decode as the strings "no"/"off", not booleans — so `enabled: no` takes the warn-and-ignore path and leaves the role ACTIVE, the opposite of the author's intent. An engineer who assumes YAML 1.1 booleans writes the fixture `enabled: no` expecting deactivation and gets a failing test against a correct implementation; one who writes `enabled: 3` never covers the trap at all. The warning's own literal is also unpinned, unlike every other new message in this spec (§2.1's `(only focus and enabled)`, §2.3's "matches no active role", §2.5's two), so item 4 can only assert "a warning happened".

resolved.evidence: §6 item 4 now pins the fixture: a quoted string (enabled: "false"), which YAML types as a string and the frontmatter parser must not coerce.

suggestion: In §2.2 pin the boundary against the parser: only a YAML boolean scalar (`true`/`false`, per yaml.v3's core schema) sets `Enabled`; every other scalar — including the strings `no`, `off`, `yes`, `"false"`, and numbers — is the non-boolean case that warns and leaves the role active. Pin the warning literal in the shape of the existing siblings (e.g. `tp.<field>.<id>.enabled is not a boolean (got %T); ignored`), and make §6 item 4 name `enabled: no` as the fixture so the highest-risk value is the one under test.

finding: Line 44 still reads "pass that set to §2.4's `skipped_roles` assembly and §2.5's refusal" — singular — while both §2.5 refusals now key on that same drop set (line 60 keys the empty-phase refusal on it, line 61 keys the `spec-coverage` one on "§2.3's drop set for the auditor phase"). Round 8's finding named this line alongside §1's cost ledger and round 9 named it again; both times it was recorded as fixed. This round finally fixed §1 ("two refusals", line 11) but left §2.3 verbatim unchanged for the third round running. §2.3 is the section that wires the drop set to its consumers, so the singular under-describes the wiring the rest of the spec depends on, and it is the sentence a reader consults to learn how many consumers the third return value has.

resolved.evidence: CONFIRMED. §2.3 now reads "both of §2.5's refusals" — the drop set has fed both for two rounds.

suggestion: "…pass that set to §2.4's `skipped_roles` assembly and to §2.5's two refusals."

finding: Clause 2 pins resolution only relative to writes, and §2.6's decision order covers only the four role-related checks, so the refusals stay unordered against the two non-writing aborts that already run earlier in `tp audit`'s emission path: `refuseAuditIfBudgetExhausted` (internal/cli/audit.go:190) and `determineAuditFiles`'s `exitAuditNoFiles` (audit.go:194, :913-919), both ahead of the first write in `loadAuditSpec` (audit.go:196). Raised in rounds 6 through 9 and each time recorded as settled by §2.6's decision order, which does not reach these two exits.

suggestion: State the precedence explicitly — e.g. the role refusals are decided after the budget and no-files aborts, so a run that would abort for either keeps its existing code and message — and add the fixture precondition to item 7's audit half.

finding: No section says what `review_roles: { regression: { enabled: false } }` does, and the spec still pulls in two directions. Non-Goal 4 (line 87) says `regression` "accepts no overrides", which implies §2.3's "matches no active role" path; §2.5's carve-out (line 60, "The built-in `regression` role does not count as an active reviewer for this check") only reads as a carve-out if `regression` is otherwise in the active reviewer set, in which case the same entry produces a drop and a `disabled-by-spec` `skipped_roles` row for a role the run then emits anyway. §2.1 advertises `enabled` on both override maps without excluding the one id the spec says must never be switched off, and item 10 tests only that `regression` fails to rescue an emptied phase. Warning, drop, or silent ignore is implementer's choice. Round 9 resolved this with "§2.1's input path is unchanged; the parse and warning behaviour is stated in §2.2" — §2.2 states neither.

resolved.evidence: §6 item 10 now pins it: regression is in neither corpus, so an entry naming it takes §2.3's "matches no active role" path — the only reading consistent with Non-Goal 4's "accepts no overrides".

suggestion: One sentence in §2.3: `regression` is appended after corpus resolution and is never in the resolver's active set, so an override entry naming it takes the "matches no active role" path and produces no drop — plus a §6 item asserting that.

finding: The empty-phase message's id list has an ambiguous referent once `domains` is in play. finding: §2.6 buffers only "the §2.3 warnings" but then asserts absolutely that a refused run writes "no prompts, no state, no warnings". The emission path produces warnings from two more sources before the checks decide: ResolveActiveCorpus returns the unknown-domain and empty-panel-fallback warnings, which the caller writes at internal/cli/review.go:657-659 (and internal/cli/audit.go around 223) before override resolution even runs, and TranslateLegacyLens's deprecation/ignored-lens warnings, which ResolveOverrideFocus folds into its own warnings slice (internal/engine/overrides.go:36-38). resolved.evidence: Moot — the buffer is deleted, so there is no buffer scope left to define. finding: Line 80 still cites "(Non-Goal 3)" for the unguarded file-deletion path — "including for `spec-coverage`, which §2.5 refuses to deactivate per spec but cannot protect from file deletion (Non-Goal 3)" — but Non-Goal 3 (line 86) is "Re-enabling a filtered role. `enabled: true` does not resurrect a role removed by `domains`", which says nothing about deletion. finding: Item 7's stated reason for the per-command artifact split — "The artifact sets differ because only `tp review` calls `EnsureReviewState`" — is wrong about the directory, and the asymmetry it justifies leaves the audit side under-guarded. `WriteSnapshotAtomic` itself does `os.MkdirAll(ReviewStateDir(specPath), 0o755)` (internal/engine/reviewstate.go:203-205), and `tp audit`'s emission path reaches it through `loadAuditSpec` (internal/cli/audit.go:196, :371), so `tp audit` creates `.tp-review/<spec>/` too. finding: Item 9 closes the `--perspective` gap by declaration rather than by test: it moves `tp review --perspective` into the excused list and ends "All five are unaffected by construction and are not asserted." The four NDJSON-positional modes are immune structurally — they never parse the spec. `--perspective` is not: it takes the spec positional and emits a prompt, and its immunity is a placement property inside the very function this change edits. In the current tree the perspective dispatch sits at internal/cli/review.go:328 and the first write (`loadReviewRoundState`) at :358, so §2.5 clause 2's hoist ("ahead of every write the emission path performs") has conforming placements on both sides of that dispatch, and only one of them preserves §2.5 clause 1. Rounds 7, 8 and 9 each reported that this immunity rests on call ordering and not on construction; the repair now asserts the opposite in the spec text, turning the one normative claim §2.5 makes about `--perspective` into a documented non-requirement.

resolved.evidence: §6 item 9 now asserts --perspective rather than excusing it: the other four are unaffected by construction, but --perspective does parse the spec and a future refactor could route it through the corpus, so it is tested.

suggestion: Keep `--perspective` out of the "unaffected by construction" sentence — give it its own clause naming the ordering requirement — and assert it in §6: `tp review --perspective regression <spec>` on the emptied-phase spec exits 0 and emits its prompt.

finding: Item 9 opens "The same spec, under the other modes that take it as the positional, never produces either §2.5 message", but item 8 has just introduced two fixtures — the unknown-id-plus-fully-deactivated spec, and "the same spec with one role left active" — and its closing sentence makes "Item 7's fixture" the nearest antecedent. Under the one-role-left-active reading the test is vacuous: that spec produces neither §2.5 message in emission mode either, so asserting their absence under `--record`/`--verify`/`--status` cannot fail no matter where the refusals are placed. Item 9's whole value is that the fixture WOULD exit 2 in emission mode, and that property is exactly what the referent leaves open — the same can't-fail shape items 7 and 8 were rewritten to avoid.

finding: §2.5 pins the empty-phase message's rendering precisely — the phase from `PhaseReviewers`/`PhaseAuditors`, "the ids sorted and comma-separated", with the example `architect, tester` — but no §6 item exercises that format. finding: Item 4 says `internal/cli/domain_lens_test.go` "exercises ResolveOverrideFocus through the CLI; moves with its new signature", and lists it under "Existing tests this change invalidates". The file never calls ResolveOverrideFocus: its only occurrence of the token is a comment at line 189 ("covered by the engine test TestResolveOverrideFocus_UnknownID"); its tests drive the built binary through runTP and assert on emitted prompts. An engine function's signature change cannot invalidate it — it compiles and passes unchanged, and its two scenarios (focus override, ghost id ignored) keep exit 0 under the new behavior. So the four-file inventory is right in count but wrong about why one of the four is on it, and it sends me looking for a call site that does not exist.
